title: Ἁλιεὺς ⟨καὶ ἰχθύες μεγάλοι καὶ βραχεῖς⟩
titleEn: The Fisherman and the Big and Little Fish
part: The Fisherman and the Big and Little Fish (Chambry 25 · Perry 282)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 25 (= Perry 282). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (⟨ ⟩ for editorial supplements). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ἁλιεὺς ἐκ τῆς θαλάσσης τὸ πρὸς ἄγραν δίκτυον ἐκβαλὼν τῶν μὲν μεγάλων ἰχθύων ἐγκρατὴς γέγονε καὶ τούτους ἐν τῇ γῇ ἥπλωσεν· οἱ δὲ βραχύτεροι τῶν ἰχθύων διὰ τῶν τρυμαλιῶν διέδρασαν ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ.
sentences.tr: Halieus ek tēs thalassēs to pros agran diktyon ekbalōn tōn men megalōn ichthyōn enkratēs gegone kai toutous en tēi gēi hēplōsen· hoi de brachyteroi tōn ichthyōn dia tōn trymaliōn diedrasan en tēi thalassēi.
sentences.l: A fisherman, having drawn the net meant for the catch out of the sea, became master of the large fish and spread these out on the land; but the smaller of the fish ran off through the meshes into the sea.
sentences.i: A fisherman drew his net up out of the sea, secured the big fish and laid them out on the shore; the smaller ones slipped through the meshes and got away into the sea.
sentences.n: τὸ πρὸς ἄγραν δίκτυον, “the net for the catch”: a prepositional phrase slipped in between article and noun, which Greek does freely and English cannot. ἐγκρατὴς γίγνομαι takes the genitive, “to become master of”; the perfect γέγονε stands in a string of aorists without much difference of force, as often in this later Greek. τρυμαλιά is a hole or perforation — here the mesh of the net. ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ after a verb of motion is “into the sea”: the old sharp distinction between ἐν and εἰς has begun to soften.

sentences.t: Ὅτι εὔκολον ἡ σωτηρία τοῖς μὴ μεγάλως εὐτυχοῦσιν, τὸν δὲ μέγαν ὄντα τῇ δόξῃ σπανίως ἴδοις ἂν ἐκφυγόντα τοὺς κινδύνους.
sentences.tr: Hoti eukolon hē sōtēria tois mē megalōs eutychousin, ton de megan onta tēi doxēi spaniōs idois an ekphygonta tous kindynous.
sentences.l: That coming off safe is easy for those not greatly prospering, but the man who is great in reputation you would rarely see having escaped the dangers.
sentences.i: The story shows that safety comes easily to those who are not greatly prosperous, but that the man great in reputation you would seldom see escape his dangers.
sentences.n: A moral in the bare Ὅτι form: the introducing verb is unexpressed in the Greek, so the literal keeps the dangling “That…” and the idiomatic supplies “the story shows”. εὔκολον ἡ σωτηρία has no verb at all — Greek leaves ἐστί out constantly. ἴδοις ἄν is a potential optative, “you would see,” the generalizing form. τῇ δόξῃ is a dative of respect, “great in respect of reputation.” σωτηρία here is nothing religious, only coming off safe.
